content_html:
The Inca Trail is one of the most famous hiking routes in the world and the best way to reach Machu Picchu through the ancient trails used by the Incas. If you're planning to take this trip in 2025, here's everything you need to know.

1. Reservations and availability

Access to the Inca Trail is regulated by the Peruvian government and only 500 people are allowed per day, including guides and porters. This means that places fill up quickly, especially in high season (May to September).

  • Book at least 6 months in advance in authorized agencies.
  • It is not allowed to travel on your own; you must hire an official agency.

2. Routes of the Inca Trail

There are several options depending on the duration and difficulty:

  • Classic Inca Trail (4 days / 3 nights): The most popular route, it runs approximately 43 km through mountains, Inca ruins and cloud forests.
  • Short Inca Trail (2 days / 1 night): Ideal for those who have less time or prefer a lighter walk.
  • Salkantay + Inca Trail (5 days / 4 nights): A more challenging alternative with spectacular landscapes.

3. Level of difficulty and preparation

The Inca Trail is not impossible, but it is challenging. The altitude (up to 4,200 m at Warmiwañusca Pass) and the multiple ascents and descents can make it physically demanding.

How to prepare:
Get used to walking long distances before the trip.
Do resistance and cardio exercises (climbing stairs helps a lot).
Acclimatize in Cusco (at least 2 days before the hike) to avoid altitude sickness.

4. What to bring?

Your travel agency will provide tents, food and essential equipment, but there are things you should bring with you:

Essentials:

  • Comfortable and light backpack (max. 5 kg if you use a carrier).
  • Thermal and light clothing (climate varies a lot).
  • Resistant trekking boots.
  • Raincoat or rain poncho.
  • Sunscreen, insect repellent and cap.
  • Trekking poles (optional, but highly recommended).

5. When to go?

Best time: From May to September (dry season, less rain and safer trails).
Rainy season: From November to March. The road is closed in February for maintenance.

6. Final experience: Arrival at Machu Picchu

The last day is magical: at dawn, you will arrive at the Puerta del Sol (Inti Punku), from where you will see Machu Picchu in all its splendor.

  • Then you will have free time to explore the citadel or climb Huayna Picchu (reserve in advance).

Finally, the easiest way to get to the city of Machupichu is by taking a tourism agency This is your moment, the adventure awaits you.
